facts.statement: The researchers used a lab-grown brain slice method with two-photon imaging to look at how synapses work.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: When the cells fired signals in a complex pattern, the light signals from individual connection points varied greatly in strength and how they changed over time.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: After the imaging, the team used electron microscopy to show that connection points leading to different structures had different functions.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: About one-quarter of the connection points led to spine structures that either released very little chemical signal or did not release any at all.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Treating the cells with specific chemicals or higher calcium levels turned the silent connection points into ones that worked normally.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The study concludes that the cells are connected by complete structures, but a missing step in preparing the chemical packets prevents them from being sent.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue
